title: assess_drift logic — deepened deterministic §3 drift classifier (Epic 8, issue #60)
prompt:
Implement assess_drift: classify whether a debater still defends its assigned side or has started agreeing with/restating the opponent. Return {captured, reason, confidence}. See docs/prds/anti-sycophancy.md.

Follow repo standards: TDD (write the failing test first, then code); max 150 lines per code file (split, don't compress); ruff = 0 violations + mypy clean; no hard-coded values (read from config); every external API call goes through the API gatekeeper (Epic 13); log via the LOG package; keep coverage >= 85%. Read docs/PRD.md and the relevant docs/prds/*.md before starting.
note: Epic 8.1 deepens the 4.4 BASELINE assess_drift into a robust deterministic classifier of the four anti-sycophancy §3 drift signals, while keeping the public assess_drift / DriftAssessment contract STABLE (4.4's test_controller_skills.py + engine test_debate_loop.py drift/nudge tests stay green). PURE/NO-NETWORK heuristic (the controller LLM may still pass explicit signals), so the API gatekeeper (Epic 13) is N/A here (noted). TDD red-first: wrote packages/core/tests/test_assess_drift.py (13 tests), watched fail (ImportError: cannot import name 'DRIFT_CAPTURE_THRESHOLD'), implemented to green. NEW module skills/_drift_logic.py: detect_drift(message, opponent_message=None) -> (confidence, labels) fires four NAMED §3 signals — (1) CONCEDE (concession phrases, weight 0.8), (2) AGREEMENT / framing-adoption ('you're right'/'i agree'/'fair point', weight 0.55), (3) HEDGE ('perhaps the opponent'/'it's true that', weight 0.5), (4) RESTATING-WITHOUT-REBUTTAL (content-token overlap with the opponent >= DRIFT_OVERLAP_THRESHOLD 0.6 AND no rebuttal/counter marker present, weight 0.7). Confidence = clamped additive sum of fired weights in [0,1] (transparent weighted scheme, NOT magic numbers); captured = confidence >= DRIFT_CAPTURE_THRESHOLD (0.5, a single configurable constant); reason = human-readable clause naming the fired signal label(s). NEW module skills/_drift_constants.py holds ALL phrase sets / rebuttal markers / weights / threshold / signal labels / reason templates as named constants (split out of constants.py, which would otherwise exceed the 150-line cap; the §3 lexicon now sits next to its detector logic). CONTRACT-STABLE extension: DriftRequest gained optional opponent_message (back-compat default None, blanks -> None); assess_drift gained a 4th optional opponent_message param — the first three positional params (message, side, signals) are unchanged, so agents/tools.py's positional _assess_drift_tool call keeps working (now forwards request.opponent_message). Caller-supplied controller signals still force capture at DRIFT_SIGNAL_CONFIDENCE (0.9) — 4.4 behaviour preserved. Removed the now-superseded 4.4 baseline constants (DRIFT_CONCESSION_PHRASES / DRIFT_PHRASE_CONFIDENCE / DRIFT_REASON_PHRASE / DRIFT_REASON_CLEAR) that the deepened detector replaced (no remaining references). Gates green locally: uv sync clean; ruff check . = All checks passed; ruff format --check . clean (158 files); mypy = no issues in 158 source files; pytest --cov = 602 passed, 100% total coverage (_drift_logic.py + _drift_constants.py + controller.py at 100%; >=85 required); check_line_limit.py rc=0 (constants.py back under 150 after the split); secret_scan.py rc=0. Files: NEW skills/_drift_logic.py, NEW skills/_drift_constants.py, NEW tests/test_assess_drift.py; EDIT skills/controller.py (assess_drift body + _join_labels helper + imports/docstring), skills/models.py (DriftRequest.opponent_message), constants.py (drop 4.4 baseline drift constants, point to the split module), agents/tools.py (forward opponent_message), docs/PROMPTS.md (8.1 entry).
